hero.title: Standing with Your Family with Dignity, Love, and Strength.
hero.subtitle: You are undertaking one of life's most meaningful journeys: and you do not walk it alone.
hero.lead: Every moment of patience and presence honors a lifetime of shared memories. This guide provides clear clinical pathways, daily care techniques, and steadfast support: step by step.
hero.disclaimer: Written for families and primary caregivers in India. Medical decisions must always be directed to a qualified neurologist.

section1A.title: What to watch for: and when to act
section1A.desc: Dementia and Alzheimer's do not begin with sudden memory loss. The earliest signs are often behavioural, easy to dismiss as stress, aging, or personality changes.

memory.heading: Repeating the same question
memory.body: Asking the same thing minutes apart: not occasionally, but consistently. Forgetting recent conversations entirely.

behaviour.heading: Sudden irritability or suspicion
behaviour.body: Unexplained anger, accusing family members of stealing, or persistent suspicion. In Indian early-onset dementia, irritability affects 61% of patients and is the most common first sign.

navigation.heading: Getting lost in familiar places
navigation.body: Unable to navigate a route walked hundreds of times. Confusion in their own neighbourhood or home.

language.heading: Struggling to find words
language.body: Pausing mid-sentence, substituting wrong words, or withdrawing from conversations to hide difficulty.

dailyTasks.heading: Unable to manage familiar tasks
dailyTasks.body: Difficulty cooking a familiar recipe, managing finances, or following routines they have followed for decades.

apathy.heading: Withdrawal and apathy
apathy.body: Loss of interest in hobbies, social withdrawal, sleeping more. Apathy affects 45% of early-onset dementia patients in India, often dismissed as depression.

judgment.heading: Poor judgment or decisions
judgment.body: Giving money to strangers, neglecting personal hygiene, making decisions that are out of character.

timePlace.heading: Confusion about time or dates
timePlace.body: Not knowing what year it is, thinking a deceased parent is still alive, or believing they are in a different decade.
